analyst_view.overall: Brentford (10th, 14 points, beaten 2-0 at Brighton last time) host Everton (7th, 16 points, three straight wins in all competitions) on Monday night, two points apart. Brentford are badly hit: Igor Thiago starts a three-match ban after his appeal failed (counted), captain Nathan Collins (knee) and Aaron Hickey (hamstring) are out for weeks after international duty, and Henry, Furo, Dasilva and Milambo are missing; Keith Andrews says Fabio Carvalho has every chance of being involved, and Callum Wilson is expected to replace Thiago. David Moyes has no new injuries and said Jack Grealish is fit and back in the group after a disciplinary absence (one preview still lists him out; most expect him on the bench), with Thierno Barry (10 goals) up front. Brentford play a lower-possession, crossing game; referee Craig Pawson (3.7 cards a game) is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals, already taking about 12.5% off Brentford for Thiago's ban. The numbers count missing players only by their goals and assists, so they barely feel the loss of two first-choice defenders, Collins and Hickey, which helps Barry and an Everton side who have scored freely of late; Carvalho's likely return also softens Brentford's attacking loss. Brentford's strong home defence and Everton's patchy away form keep this mild: about 2.5.

corners.text: The numbers say 10 corners, already counting Brentford's low recent corner count (21 in six) and Everton's slightly higher one. Brentford cross a lot from wide (about 18 a game) with Lewis-Potter or Diouf filling in for Hickey on the left, and Everton's 4-2-3-1 is their usual shape, so I stay at 10.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.2 cards, already lowered for referee Craig Pawson (3.7 a game) and calm past meetings. Everton have no suspensions or injuries and there is no needle between the sides beyond a tight table, so I stay at 3.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.6 shots, already raising Everton for their recent volume (81 shots in six). Brentford lose Thiago's shooting but Wilson starts up front and Carvalho may return, while a weakened Brentford back line should let Everton, who average about 15 shots a game, shoot a little more; the two balance, so 27.6.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.2 shots on target, already lowering Brentford for poor recent accuracy (19 on target in six). Losing Thiago's finishing is offset by Wilson leading the line and Barry facing a back four without Collins and Hickey, so I stay at 8.2.
